snippet.title: From Latin America to Europe - The dangerous schemes of human traffickers | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Women in Latin America are recruited with brutal methods, then enslaved in Europe. A survivor recounts how she was lured to Spain with the promise of a job, then forced into prostitution.

A young woman from Latin America applies to a modeling agency in Spain. Flight, accommodation—everything is paid for. But when she arrives, her papers are taken away and she is forced into sex work, first in Spain, then in Germany. The reason given: she had to repay the travel expenses. Only the police can free her, during an undercover operation.
Sebastian Eichler from the Mainz Criminal Investigation Department conducts his investigations as follows: He responds to online ads as a fake client, then reveals himself as a police officer during the appointed meetings. "It’s like looking for a needle in a haystack,” says Eichler, "to take action against the perpetrators, we need the women’s statements.”
But often, the women remain silent out of fear. Because the perpetrators not only pressure the women, but also threaten to harm family members back home.
Human rights organizations and law enforcement agencies are monitoring this phenomenon. They suspect that the narcos — Colombian drug cartels—have now entered the business. In Spain, Carmen Gonzalez of the Policia Nacional reports initial successes. Her special unit has managed to dismantle a network.
Manuela Schon and her team from the Women’s Affairs Department of the City of Wiesbaden note that more and more women are being offered for sex in private apartments and hotels. For them, a ban on the purchase of sex based on the Swedish model would be the solution. There, clients are severely punished, while the women remain unpunished. France also follows this abolitionist model. Yet human trafficking occurs there as well.
In Vienna, the UN Special Representative on Organized Crime has convened the first international congress for victims of human trafficking. Over 30 survivors recount their stories and identify the root causes: poverty, displacement, and gender inequality.

snippet.title: Examining U.S.-Saudi Ties | The Crown Prince & the President (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
Martin Smith examines the alliance between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and President Donald Trump in this 90-minute documentary. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

What is behind the alliance between President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS), and what are the ramifications for the U.S., Saudi Arabia and the Middle East as a whole? 

Answers unfold in “The Crown Prince & the President,” the latest documentary from an award-winning team that includes directors, writers and producers Martin Smith and Marcela Gaviria, and co-producers Scott Anger and Jennifer Brooks. 
 
“‘The Crown Prince & the President’ is based on over 100 interviews I have done in the U.S. and abroad,” says Smith, who also serves as correspondent and has covered the U.S.-Saudi relationship for more than 20 years. “Our investigation is an incisive look at the forces binding the two men and their countries together, and what each stands to gain — from ambitions for a new Middle East, to arms deals, investments and personal profit.”
 
Over the course of the documentary, that story is told with insights from former U.S. officials and diplomats, members of the Saudi government, Trump administration insiders, Saudi dissidents, human rights and foreign policy experts, and journalists who have covered financial ties between the Trump family and Saudi Arabia. 
 
What emerges is a sharp chronicle of how the alliance between the crown prince who promised reform and the Trump administration has grown, despite MBS’ crackdown on dissent and the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi, in which MBS denied involvement.
 
The documentary also offers a powerful examination of the Trump administration’s foreign policy strategy for Saudi Arabia, and the implications for the surrounding region, the U.S. and the world.
 
“The Crown Prince & the President” is a FRONTLINE production with Rain Media. The correspondent is Martin Smith. The co-producers are Scott Anger and Jennifer Brooks. The writers, producers and directors are Marcela Gaviria & Martin Smith. The managing editor of FRONTLINE is Andrew Metz. The editor-in-chief and executive producer of FRONTLINE is Raney Aronson-Rath.

snippet.title: The mystery of primitive Earth | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Could life on Earth have emerged many times before it thrived? 🌋🌊  

The origin of life on Earth remains one of science’s greatest mysteries. However, some scientists believe that life may have emerged several times on early Earth but did not always succeed in becoming established.  

Primitive Earth was marked by extreme conditions: active volcanoes, forming oceans, and an atmosphere very different from today’s.  

In that chaotic environment, water, minerals, and heat created the chemical conditions necessary for life to emerge. The real turning point, however, was not just its emergence, but its ability to persist, adapt and evolve, eventually transforming the planet into the habitable world we know today.

snippet.title: For-Profit Adoptions & Misconduct Allegations (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS) + Retro Report
snippet.description:
With Retro Report, an investigation into how so-called “baby brokers” have targeted pregnant women and families looking to adopt, and an epicenter of the problem in Utah.

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

The adoption industry in the U.S. is a multi-billion-dollar business, where demand outpaces the number of infants available for adoption. In “Baby Brokers,” FRONTLINE and Retro Report investigate a loosely-regulated corner of the industry described as “adoption tourism” and examine how allegations of misconduct involving for-profit agencies and brokers have mounted. 

The documentary illuminates a patchwork system, where allegations of misconduct have stacked up in states like Utah with historically more permissive laws. 

In the documentary, the head of an adoption agency in Utah says that out-of-state adoptions fulfill an important need. But other sources express concern about how brokers and agencies have used cash and housing offers as incentives for vulnerable women in other states.

In recent months, Utah has moved to tighten some of its laws in response to mounting criticisms from birth mothers, their advocates, and adoptive parents. And at the federal level, lawmakers from a number of states are backing a bipartisan bill aimed at reining in unlicensed brokers who funnel pregnant women and families across state lines for adoptions.

As the debate over “adoption tourism” continues, “Baby Brokers” is a must-watch exploration of the practice, the role of brokers, and the impact on both birth mothers and adoptive parents.

snippet.title: The Fall of the Ottoman Empire: Why the Middle East Still Burns Today
snippet.description:
After World War I, the victorious powers of Britain and France dismantled the centuries-old Ottoman Empire and redrew the map of the Middle East. Secret wartime agreements, broken promises, and imperial ambitions transformed entire regions overnight. Arab leaders who fought alongside the Allies expected independence, while Zionists were promised a homeland in Palestine through the Balfour Declaration. Behind closed doors, diplomats carved up Syria, Iraq, Palestine, and Anatolia with borders whose consequences continue to shape global politics more than a century later.

As the Treaty of Sèvres attempted to divide the Ottoman world, resistance movements erupted across the collapsing empire. In Anatolia, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk led a brutal war against invading Greek forces and the Allied-backed settlement, laying the foundations of modern Turkey. From the destruction of Smyrna and the forced population exchanges between Greeks and Turks to the shattered hopes of Kurdish and Arab independence, the documentary traces how the end of the Ottoman Empire unleashed conflicts, nationalism, and political instability that still define the Middle East today.

snippet.title: Illegitimate children in Iran - Invisible and without rights | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Leyla loves her daughter Nila more than anything. But there’s a problem: according to Iranian law, Nila does not exist. Because she is an illegitimate child, she has no papers or rights. Mother and daughter must fight the absurd rules of a disingenuous regime.

But the resourceful duo refuse to give up. They hope to become part of Iranian society and save Nila from a life in hiding. "Nila's Dream in the Garden of Eden" accompanies Leyla in her struggle to achieve recognition of her daughter Nila's identity. Until then, she cannot obtain papers, go to school or receive medical care. The doors of Iranian society are closed to her.

Leyla and Nila desperately try to escape this cycle and free themselves from life in the shadows. They fight against bureaucratic hurdles and the opaque rules of an arbitrary state that is blind to the fate of a child. Despite everything, they manage to remain optimistic - they paint, sing, dance and fantasize about great journeys, a jet-set life of luxury and a miraculous twist of fate. They are a living example of how dreams and hopes can defy even the bleakest circumstances.

Film director Niloufar Taghizadeh knows Leyla from her school days. Years later, she learns of Leyla’s story, and a fate shaped by an absurd loophole in Iranian law. Driven by the desire to change the lives of the two, as well as that of many other undocumented children in Iran, she embarks on a risky journey to make this film. For almost three years, she accompanies the pair and films, partly undercover, in Iranian government offices and behind closed doors with decision-makers in the system to tell a story that, officially at least, doesn’t exist.

snippet.title: America's war for freedom - 250 years of independence | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
In 1776, America was torn: between loyalty to the British Crown, and its own desire for independence. 250 years later, digitized eyewitness accounts provide insights into daily life during the War of Independence for the first time.

Newly transcribed pension claims from the United States’ National Archives bring to life the experiences of people during the American War of Independence, between 1775 and 1783. They recount how they fought, suffered, and persevered despite great hardships - inspired by the words of the Founding Fathers and under the leadership of George Washington, who, as commander-in-chief, led the American troops to victory over the British. When signing the Declaration of Independence in 1776, the stakes could not have been higher: Had the uprising failed, every soldier and every delegate would have faced charges of treason and death.
The documentary shows that the founding of the American republic was shaped not only by famous figures, but by countless courageous voices whose stories are only now coming to light.

Why did 22-year-old militiaman William French take up arms after the first shots were fired at Lexington and Concord? Men like James Potter Collins describe the chaos of battles such as Bunker Hill, Brandywine, Long Island, and Yorktown. Women like Deborah Sampson fight on the front lines in disguise, while others, like Susannah Chandler, protect their families at home. Veteran soldiers like John Boudy risk everything, as do the rebel armies in the South. Enslaved people like Prince Griswold place their lives at stake.

After the victory, the values of the Declaration of Independence (with ideals such as "life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness”) spread like wildfire - yet for many who fought, the promise of freedom remains unfulfilled.

snippet.title: Germany's Underworld: From the Alps to the River Rhine
snippet.description:
Unlock the secrets of Germany’s rivers and lakes—discover bizarre animals, hidden caves, and epic freshwater predators in this stunning underwater journey!

Dive deep beneath the surface as we explore Germany’s mysterious aquatic world, from the snowy peaks of the Alps to the tidal reaches of the North Sea. Discover rare footage of diverse fish like the mighty northern pike and elusive Welsh catfish, delicate courtships, journeys of glacial meltwater, and ancient underwater relics. Venture through clear lakes such as Königsee and Lake Constance, uncovering extraordinary wildlife, from invasive jellyfish to prehistoric settlements, and learn how human activity has shaped this fragile ecosystem.

Follow the winding path of the Rhine as it carves dramatic gorges, waterfalls, and hidden canyons, home to curious salamanders, ancient fossils, and dazzling dragonflies. Reveal the wonders of submerged caves in the Swabian Alps, inhabited only by the bravest divers and rarest species. Witness fascinating natural cycles: mass frog and toad gatherings, unique breeding rituals, and the seasonal return of cranes as winter’s chill sets in. 

This documentary showcases the delicate balance of life underwater, evolutionary marvels, and the enduring impact of both nature and humans on these vibrant but threatened habitats. Perfect for fans of wildlife, ecology, and natural wonders, this is Germany as you’ve never seen it before—through the eyes of its remarkable waters.

snippet.title: Marilyn Monroe Cold Case: What Really Happened? | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
In August 1962, America loses its blonde angel: Marilyn Monroe dies under mysterious circumstances. The official cause of death: "probably suicide". But this is more than doubtful. Her dying is as contradictory as she herself: Marilyn was dazzling and insecure, glamorous and unhappy, a puritanical soul who sold sex and became the projection screen for generations. What did really happen? After her housekeeper discovers her body, six hours pass before the police are called - officers find a beautifully draped body, sleeping pills in the blood but no pill residue in the stomach, unsure-looking witnesses. Today, there are no police files to be found. Several men play shadow roles in this drama: Marilyn's psychiatrist and two of the most powerful men in the world at the time: Romancers John F. and Bobby Kennedy.

snippet.title: The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS) + El Faro
snippet.description:
What was behind Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele’s deal with President Donald Trump to imprison deportees from the U.S. at CECOT? FRONTLINE and El Faro investigate. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

Three months into President Donald Trump’s second term, President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador opened the doors of his country’s notorious prison, CECOT, for deportees the Trump administration had swept up and accused of being gang members. Despite revelations that most of the men had no criminal convictions in the U.S. or proven gang affiliations, as well as concerns about harsh treatment, both presidents touted the move as a win.

In “The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador,” FRONTLINE and reporters from the El Salvador news outlet El Faro investigate what was behind the controversial deal, and what each leader stood to gain. 

Through interviews with current and former U.S. officials, reporters and insiders, the documentary shines new light on Bukele’s tangled history with the gangs the U.S. is fighting, why Bukele offered to imprison U.S. deportees, and who he asked be returned to El Salvador from U.S. custody in exchange, in what one reporter calls “a deal within a deal.”

Ancient crimes, mysterious disasters, and ruthless rulers: this documentary reopens some of history’s oldest cold cases using modern forensic science and archaeology. In ancient Athens, researchers investigate the shocking discovery of 450 dead babies hidden deep inside a well beneath the Agora, searching for evidence of mass murder, disease, or forgotten burial rituals. In imperial Rome, fire experts reconstruct the devastating Great Fire of 64 AD to determine whether Emperor Nero truly burned his own capital or became the victim of political propaganda.

The documentary also explores the radical religious revolution of Akhenaten in ancient Egypt, where temples were desecrated and the traditional gods replaced with a single sun cult. Combining experimental archaeology, forensic medicine, psychology, and historical analysis, this episode of Crime Scene: Antiquity reveals how modern science can finally solve mysteries that have remained unsolved for thousands of years.

snippet.title: War Factories: S03 EP04
snippet.description:
Think Porsche only means speed? Discover the secret history of Porsche in WWII tank design and the epic war of industrial production that shaped modern warfare.

Step inside the untold story of war production, where victory on the battlefield depended not just on military strategy, but on factory power. This video exposes how brands like Porsche, Skoda, and Rolls-Royce were forged in the fire of world wars—not just in racing circuits. Dive into the surprising journey of Ferdinand Porsche, who began as a pioneering electrical engineer and race car designer but became obsessed with crafting military muscle for the Nazi war machine. From the iconic Volkswagen Beetle to the notorious Panzer VIII Maus, see how Porsche’s ambition and partnership with Hitler led to engineering marvels—and catastrophic failures—for Germany’s war efforts.

Explore the innovation and missteps behind vehicles like the Kubelwagen, Ferdinand, Elephant, and JagdTiger, and learn how Porsche’s relentless pursuit of bigger, more powerful tanks ironically helped the Allies by draining Nazi resources. This video details the critical production battles of WWII—from the German struggle with mass manufacturing to the Soviet T-34’s game-changing design—and reveals why tank quality sometimes couldn’t match the importance of sheer quantity. Finally, trace how Porsche’s wartime legacy evolved into the legendary sports cars we know today, thanks to Ferry Porsche and the iconic 356 and 911 models. If you think you know Porsche, think again—this is the story of genius, ambition, and the high price of overengineering in the crucible of war.

snippet.title: War Factories: S03 EP05
snippet.description:
Modern wars aren’t won on the battlefield—they’re won in the factories. Discover how mass production, the Opel Blitz, and American industry shaped WWII’s outcome.

Dive deep into the hidden history of war production, where trucks—not tanks—became the unsung heroes of World War II. This video unpacks the incredible story of the Opel Blitz truck, its vital role in enabling Blitzkrieg, and the unexpected American connection: General Motors owned and operated Opel, Germany’s largest truck manufacturer, before and during Hitler’s rise. You’ll learn how GM, Ford, and other industrial titans navigated a complex web of politics, profit, and power struggles, sometimes supplying both sides of the war.

We trace the rise of German war manufacturing—from GM’s risky investment in Opel through the company’s transformation under Nazi rule. Uncover the brilliance of mass production at Brandenburg’s truck plant, the crucial role of synthetic fuels (with GM’s involvement), and the moral dilemmas and evasions faced by Allied corporations caught in wartime Germany. See how the humble truck became the backbone of modern warfare, why supply chains could decide victory or defeat, and how, ultimately, America’s unrivaled industrial capacity helped tip the scales against Hitler. Learn how GM and Ford factories turned out armies of trucks, tanks, and planes for both the Axis and Allies, and how postwar justice unfolded for foreign companies like GM.

Whether you’re fascinated by military history, the economics of war, or stories of corporate intrigue, this video offers a sweeping, nuanced look at the real engines of the Second World War.

snippet.title: D-Day, Normandy 1944: The Espionage Plot That Changed WW2 | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
June 6, 1944: nearly 130,000 Allied soldiers land on the beaches of Normandy in the largest amphibious invasion in history. But long before the first troops reached France, a secret war of deception was already underway. This documentary reveals how British intelligence and a network of double agents helped mislead Adolf Hitler and the German High Command in the crucial weeks before D-Day. Through Operation Fortitude, MI5 operatives created fake armies, false radio traffic, and carefully controlled intelligence designed to convince the Nazis that the real invasion would come at Pas-de-Calais instead of Normandy.

Featuring legendary spies such as Juan Pujol Garcia, code-named “Garbo,” this documentary uncovers the extraordinary espionage campaign that helped change the course of World War II. From double agents and deception networks to secret operations that fooled Hitler himself, this is the untold story behind the success of D-Day.

snippet.title: Displaced on Java - A village battling rising sea levels | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
In 2014, the first flood caught the sleeping residents of the Javanese village off guard. Since then, rising sea tides have kept engulfing the village. The water is still rising — up to 15 centimeters in a year.

So far, the residents of the village of Timbulsloko in Java have been able to keep pace with the rising sea levels by building their homes on higher ground. How long can that go on for? Where once roads and vast rice fields stood, there's now nothing but water. The ocean has carved deep into the land, washing away everything in its path: Homes, gardens, mangrove forests. For generations, people here lived mainly from rice farming. Now they fish, and are experimenting with aquaculture. At high tide, the water in some homes comes up to your knees. The villagers have moved their beds and built walkways to make it possible for them to stay. The ocean is even claiming the cemetery as it moves in on the isolated village, eroding it piece by piece. Residents here are struggling to contain the impacts. How long can they stop the water from disrupting their day-to-day living? At which point will they be forced to leave?

snippet.title: President Trump’s Pressure Campaign on the Federal Reserve (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An examination of President Donald Trump’s unprecedented attempts to assert control over the most powerful institution in the U.S. economy: the Federal Reserve.

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

“The President vs. the Fed” illuminates the roots and stakes of President Trump’s battle with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the independence of the country’s central bank and its policy decisions.

As the documentary reports, Congress designed the Fed to be insulated from political interference so it would be free to act in the long-term interest of the economy, including by making at-times unpopular monetary policy decisions. But Trump allies argue the Fed’s independence has shielded it from accountability for its mistakes and that Trump was within his rights to try to force Powell out.

With clarity and precision, “The President vs. the Fed” examines where the battle stands now and how — with inflation on the rise amid the effects of the Iran war and Trump tariff fallout — the Fed led by Powell’s successor Kevin Warsh will likely face not only a tricky political landscape but an economic one as well.

“The President vs. the Fed” is a FRONTLINE production with Left/Right Docs. The director and correspondent is James Jacoby. The producers and writers are Anya Bourg and James Jacoby. The senior producer is Frank Koughan. The managing editor of FRONTLINE is Andrew Metz. The editor-in-chief and executive producer of FRONTLINE is Raney Aronson-Rath.

snippet.description:
Before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, Dmytro “Dok” Dokunov was a filmmaker living in an eco-community. While documenting his life, he was drafted into a combat unit of the Ukrainian Armed Forces and sent to the front. During the Kherson campaign, several of his comrades were killed. Promoted to commander, he was later deployed to the city of Bakhmut, where he was injured in urban combat, while many others never returned.  

More than 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed since the start of the war, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and many remain missing. Those still fighting on the front lines carry countless invisible wounds of war. The psychological toll, and how soldiers cope with trauma, is of growing concern.

And in order to solve the mystery, they follow up on historical sources and use state-of-the-art technology to try to uncover new unexplored paths.
